title: Unified capability manifest endpoint for per-version profiles
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Background: As new model families and variants are onboarded we need a single, stable API surface that exposes both per-model capability flags and per-version published performance profiles (limits, context windows, feature gates, and representative perf metrics). Current model catalog endpoints are fragmented: some fields live in the manifest, others in experimental profile tables, and clients must stitch versions together. This ticket proposes a new /models/{model_id}/manifest endpoint (manifest = capability+versioned-profiles) that is backward-compatible and optimized for SDK consumption and runtime routing decisions. Goals: 1) Provide authoritative per-version profiles so routing and pinning policies can choose compatible fallbacks. 2) Include machine-readable capability flags (e.g., streaming, function_calling, structured_output). 3) Publish performance signals (latency p50/p95, throughput baseline, recommended batch sizes) to support cost/latency policies. 4) Keep the schema compact and stable; support incremental extension via manifest_version field.
acceptance_criteria: New endpoint GET /v1/models/{model_id}/manifest returns manifest_version and a list of versions with profile objects
Profile object includes context_window, max_tokens_per_request, feature_flags, limits (token/min, bytes), and perf_estimates (latency_p50_ms, latency_p95_ms, baseline_throughput_tps)
Endpoint supports optional ?stable_only=true to return only versions flagged stable
SDKs (js/py) are updated to add convenience getter and do not break existing /models endpoints
Automated migration tests validate backward compatibility for existing clients that read model catalog fields
changes_summary: Add a single manifest endpoint that aggregates capability flags and per-version performance profiles. Introduces manifest_version for schema evolution, version entries with profile fields for limits, context_window, feature_flags, and perf_estimates. Adds a stable_only query parameter and a small set of feature flags to drive routing and client behavior. No change to existing /models listing behavior; existing fields remain for compatibility.
migration_plan: Phase 1: Implement endpoint as read-only aggregation of existing catalog tables; return manifest_version=v1
Phase 2: Add SDK getters and deprecate direct reads of scattered profile fields in docs with a 6-week notice
Phase 3: Start populating perf_estimates for new onboarded models only, then backfill high-usage models
Phase 4: Enable routing policies to prefer stable versions via a feature flag toggle; monitor for regressions
test_plan: Unit tests for serializer and schema validation for manifest_version v1
Integration tests: end-to-end manifest generation for 10 representative models (meta, gpt-like, local quantized)
Backward compatibility tests: ensure existing /models responses are unchanged for 30 sample clients
Load test: 10k rps on manifest endpoint with cached responses and verify tail latency under 50ms for 95th pct with CDN layer
monitoring_and_rollout: Start canary: roll out manifest read to 5% of traffic for 72h; track errors and response time
Add tracing hooks: include model_id and version in traces and measure mean serialization time
Create console dashboard: manifest-v1 adoption, per-model perf_estimates variance vs actual, client error rates
Rollback plan: disable manifest in gateway and fall back to previous catalog endpoints if errors > 1% over 15m
notes: Trade-offs: packing perf_estimates into manifest simplifies client routing but will increase catalog payload size; mitigated by caching and stable_only filter.
Open question: canonical units for perf_estimates (ms and tokens/sec) were agreed but we need final verification against runtime telemetry team
We deliberately avoid embedding quantization/weight-format details in v1 to prevent contract churn; those may live in a separate file linked by manifest
